hypotheses.justification: The proof uses `[L.NeBot]` in only one place: the final branch calls `stronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto`, which requires `[NeBot u]`. The statement still holds when `L.filter = ⊥`, so we can split on `L.NeBot`. If it holds, the existing proof goes through unchanged. If it fails, `tprod_bot` (Topology/Algebra/InfiniteSum/Defs.lean, which takes `hL : ¬L.NeBot`) rewrites `∏'[L] i, f i` to `∏ᶠ i, f i`. Here the finite product is taken in the monoid `X → E`. Next, `finprod_def'` (or `finprod_def`) gives two cases. If the multiplicative support is finite, the result is a `Finset` product of the functions `mulIndicator (f i)`, and each of these is `f i` or `1`. That product is strongly measurable by `Finset.stronglyMeasurable_prod`, which needs only `[ContinuousMul E]`, together with `h` and `stronglyMeasurable_one`. If the support is infinite, the result is `1`, which is strongly measurable by `stronglyMeasurable_one`. This is the same reasoning as the first two branches of the current proof, none of which uses `NeBot`. The `h.choose` branch of `tprod_def` can never be reached in the `⊥` case, because `HasProd f 1 L` always holds there (`hasProd_bot`). So the theorem stays true and provable without `[L.NeBot]`.
